newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 23.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Monday:

* The United States and other countries are asking Canada to be a partner in an effort to remove Khmer Rouge leader, Pol Pot, out of Cambodia and put him before an international tribunal for crimes against humanity.
* The leaders of the eight countries who met at a summit this past weekend in Denver issued a laundry list of proposals from seeking democratic elections in Hong Kong to new aid for Africa.
* U.S. President Bill Clinton said the tobacco settlement is solely a beginning, not an end, and said he beileved it could harm the government's regulation of nicotine.

* The National Association for the Advancement of Colored People is rethinking its longstanding push for integration of public schools, and is now considering focusing more heavily on improvement of majority-black schools.
* Federal housing officials are nowing admitting that the landlords of some subsidized housing units got wealthy at the expense of their tenants.
* Rural New Jersey communities are feeling left out of a state Supreme Court order that Gov. Christie Todd Whitman send an additional $248 million to poor urban schools.
* Scores of women over 40, who weren't around for passage of Title IX, are finding they too have a competitive spirit in athletics.
